article_title: Better P-curves: Making P-curve analysis more robust to errors, fraud, and ambitious P-hacking, a Reply to Ulrich and Miller (2015).
citation: Simonsohn, U., Simmons, J. P., & Nelson, L. D. (2015). Better P-Curves: Making P-Curve Analysis More Robust To Errors, Fraud, and Ambitious P-Hacking, A Reply To Ulrich and Miller (2015). Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 144(6), 1146–1152. https://doi.org/10.1037/xge0000104
title: P-curve analysis: the distribution of significant p values diagnoses evidential value, null results, and p-hacking
description: P-curve analysis is a tool for assessing whether a set of statistically significant findings contains evidential value. It examines the distribution of significant p values: "True effects, those that differ from zero, lead to right-skewed p-curves (e.g., more .01s than .04s). Nonexistent effects lead to flat p-curves". Many forms of p-hacking lead to left-skewed p-curves, so a right-skewed observed p-curve rules out selective reporting of significant results as the sole explanation.
requirements: Included p values must test the hypothesis of interest, have a uniform distribution under the null, and be statistically independent of other p values
constraints: The framework assumes that among significant results, the magnitude of the p value does not affect whether it gets reported
target_learners: researchers conducting or evaluating p-curve analyses
target_learning_goals: assessing whether a set of published studies contains evidential value
examples: The authors applied p-curve to a set of JPSP experiments reported only with a covariate, observing a significantly left-skewed p-curve
key_sources: Simonsohn, U., Simmons, J. P., & Nelson, L. D. (2015). Better P-Curves: Making P-Curve Analysis More Robust To Errors, Fraud, and Ambitious P-Hacking, A Reply To Ulrich and Miller (2015). Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 144(6), 1146–1152. https://doi.org/10.1037/xge0000104

article_title: Better performance of medical students on pharmacotherapy knowledge and skills tests is associated with practising with e-learning program P-scribe.
citation: Kalfsvel L, Versmissen J, van Doorn A, van den Broek W, van der Kuy H, van Rosse F. (2022). Better performance of medical students on pharmacotherapy knowledge and skills tests is associated with practising with e‐learning program P‐scribe. Br J Clin Pharmacol. https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.15077
title: P-scribe e-learning platform for pharmacotherapy education
description: P-scribe is a Dutch web-based e-learning platform for pharmacy and medical students, used at all Dutch university medical centres and several Belgian medical centres. E-learning modules can be built adapted to curriculum needs and are based around the WHO 6-step model for rational pharmacotherapy. Students are "guided through different life‐like cases in which a change in pharmacotherapy is needed", each module focusing on a different aspect such as side-effects or polypharmacy. At Erasmus MC it is used in the medical master's curriculum as part of flipped classroom teaching.
requirements: Modules are developed by medical doctors and pharmacists working as clinical pharmacotherapy teachers
Students have personal accounts with data tracking enabled
constraints: Data tracking records the time the module was open on the computer, not how much time the student actually spent on it
examples: At Erasmus MC, e-learning modules are used in the master's curriculum as part of flipped classroom teaching, with compulsory and non-compulsory modules embedded throughout
